label: prf:bar-apply-transfer
title: Proof of bar apply transfer
html:
Proof. (1) Assume \forall q > a,\, P(q). Let q < a^{-1} with q > 0. Then q^{-1} > a, so P(q^{-1}) holds, which implies P(q) by bar-invariance. The reverse implication is dual. (3) Negate (1). (2) This is false in general. For example, P(q) = \mathbf{1}_{q \in (a, a^{-1})} is bar-invariant on (a, a^{-1}) but false outside. Under continuity, every limit point of \{q : P(q)\} is bar-conjugate to a limit point of \neg P, forcing the symmetric extension. \square

The bar-transfer principle establishes that a one-sided substrate bound for a bar-invariant property yields the bar-conjugate bound. If we prove

  q_0 > 1/\varphi^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{E}_{q_0}\text{ is non-degenerate}

then bar-applying yields

  q_0 < \varphi^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{E}_{1/q_0}\text{ is non-degenerate}

The property holds on the super-classical wing (1, \varphi^2) exactly as established on the sub-classical wing (1/\varphi^2, 1). We fold both derivations into a single statement on the bar-self-dual band \mathcal{B} = (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2).

Every two-sided stability statement of the form

  q \in (a, a^{-1}) \Longleftrightarrow \text{stable}

with a bar-invariant stability condition requires proving only one inequality. The companion inequality is automatic. We apply this to the following eligible bar-invariant predicates:

  • \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) < 0 (single real component), via bar T-duality.
  • Slater-strict feasibility of the confinement SDP formulated \iota-equivariantly in q.
  • Markov-trace positivity on the Hecke algebra (\sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}).
  • j-invariant finiteness of the Descartes elliptic curve.
